title: First night under King Oliver's name: the band gets drunk in Hayes, Kansas
summary: At their first dance under King Oliver's name, several players got drunk on homemade drink, and Oliver nearly dismissed them; Phillips and others scolded them.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Back to King Oliver again. Anything else...

Well, let me tell you this about King Oliver. The first night that we played with King Oliver, when King Oliver took the band over, we went to a little old town called... I think it was Hayes, Kansas.
You were talking about Hayes, Kansas.

Yeah. We went out to play this dance that night. King almost was going to let us go, wasn't going to be bothered with us. All the cats got drunk! Ha-ha! I didn't get drunk, Pete didn't get drunk, and who else...?
Was Lester in the band at that time?

No, no. This was Bronson's band. This was the band and he was taking it over. It was the first night that it was under King's name. Pat, they got drunk... About five or six of them went out there drinking. They had a drink out there in Kansas they called chalk, and something like (?). So it would make you higher than four buildings. High up there. So these cats all before the dance went to this cat's house that made it. And he made us all high. Now, Francis Whitby, he got so drunk that he was on the bandstand... That's what he was doing. So everybody said, "King Oliver's band,

all of them got drunk tonight." You know, we was playing all right, pretty good, but of course, when we got drunk, we started jamming. Didn't try to play no music. All them cats couldn't read no music, high and drunk as they was. Whitby, he was out; Hap, he was drunk; Charlie Toran, the piano player, he was drunk.

So King said, "Well, I'll be damned! I'm here taking the band over, and all these cats done got drunk on me. If they start off this way, what the hell they gonna do in the season?" So we got together on them, and we cussed them out, we did. I cussed a lot of them out, Pete did, Jack Holt, Sam -- we give 'em hell, you know what I mean. For gettin' drunk, you know what I mean? They went out there and got drunk, man. It was disgraceful. On the bandstand... Here's a cat laying up on the bandstand this-a-way. That chalk had knocked them out. Made them high, and the next day they were sick, too. But didn't nothin' happen like that no more, though.

But King, he told me about a lot of things... He used to tell all of us while we'd be riding in the bus. He said, "Man, you cats sho disgusted me. When I got back from Wichita" (we came back from Wichita) "I was gettin' ready to tell you all to go, man -- go for yourself. Forget about it." Sure did!
